# Morse — The signal studio

A browser-based, privacy-first Morse translator and personal cipher studio.

## Main pages
- / — Overview
- /encoder — Text to Morse with audio, light, vibration and tap-key input
- /decoder — Morse to text
- /alphabet — International Morse reference and app-specific Arabic/Urdu extensions
- /cipher — Emoji codebook (obfuscation) and AES-256-GCM encryption
- /practice — Morse recognition quiz\n- /about — About Morse Studio

## Privacy and security
- Text conversion and cryptographic operations run locally in the browser.
- No account, content analytics or message backend is required.
- Codebook mode is obfuscation, not encryption.
- Secure mode uses AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations, a random 16-byte salt and 12-byte nonce.
- The application does not store passphrases. Saved codebooks are encrypted at rest with a user-provided passphrase.

## Limitations
- Arabic/Urdu character mappings are app-specific extensions and are not represented as a universal official Morse standard.
- Browser audio, vibration and light output depend on device support and permissions.
- Cipher links with secrets in URL fragments should be treated as bearer secrets; anyone with the full link can access its contents/key.
